title: Renewables Go Local in Developing Markets | BloombergNEF
gist: Renewable-energy investment in low- and middle-income economies (excluding mainland China) hit a record $140 billion in 2025 even as global wind/solar investment peaked in 2024, and 68% of that 2025 funding came from capital providers operating inside those same economies rather than from wealthy-nation transfers. Deployment stays highly concentrated — India, Brazil and Turkey took 52% of the $412 billion disclosed over 2016-2025 — and private investors supply roughly 85% of asset finance.

themes.theme: Record EM deployment despite a global investment peak

insights.claim: Capital deployed into renewable energy in low- and middle-income economies reached a record $140 billion in 2025, even though global wind and solar investment overall peaked a year earlier in 2024.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: A global clean-energy capex peak masks an emerging-market boom, so headline 'renewables slowdown' narratives misprice where equipment demand is still growing.
insights.quote: While global wind/solar investment peaked in 2024, capital deployed in low- and middle-income economies hit a record $140 billion in 2025, with more nations than ever receiving funds from abroad.

insights.claim: Total new-build utility-scale renewable investment in low- and middle-income economies excluding mainland China, with disclosed capital providers, was $412 billion over 2016-2025.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Sets the addressable size of the developing-market renewables financing pool over a full decade, excluding undisclosed deals.
insights.quote: $412 billion: Total 2016-2025 new-build utility-scale investment in renewable projects in low- and middle-income economies (excluding mainland China) with disclosed capital providers

themes.theme: Capital is going local, not north-south

insights.claim: The rise in clean-energy investment across developing economies is not primarily a story of wealthier nations increasing their generosity; in many cases middle-income economies are proving to be their own major sources of capital.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Reframes climate-finance politics: developing-market build-out is less hostage to donor-country budgets and aid cycles than commonly assumed.
insights.quote: But this is not primarily a “north-south” story of wealthier nations upping their generosity. Rather, in many cases middle-income economies themselves are proving to be their own major sources of capital.

insights.claim: In 2025, 68% of all funding for renewable projects in low- and middle-income markets came from capital providers operating within those same economies.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Local banks, sponsors and institutional pools are now the marginal financier, so domestic rates and currency conditions matter more than global concessional flows.
insights.quote: A total of 68% of all funding for projects in low- and middle-income markets came from sources operating within those economies in 2025.

insights.claim: Six of the 10 largest provider markets of renewable asset finance are themselves middle-income economies, together supplying about 48% of total disclosed asset finance.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Middle-income countries are now roughly half the supply side of developing-market clean-energy capital, a structural shift in who underwrites the transition.
insights.quote: Six of the 10 largest provider markets are middle-income, supplying about 48% of total disclosed asset finance.

insights.claim: India, Brazil and Turkey together received 52% of disclosed renewable utility-scale investment in low- and middle-income markets excluding mainland China over 2016-2025.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: On a dollar basis the developing-market renewables trade is really a three-country trade, concentrating both opportunity and policy risk.
insights.quote: India, Brazil and Turkey received 52% of disclosed renewable utility-scale investment over 2016-2025, while India alone accounted for 29%.

insights.claim: India alone absorbed 29% of disclosed utility-scale renewable investment into low- and middle-income markets over the 2016-2025 decade.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Nearly a third of a decade's developing-market renewables capital hinges on one country's policy, tariff and grid outcomes.

themes.theme: Private capital dominates; DFIs matter only at the bottom of the income ladder

insights.claim: Private investors supply about 85% of renewable asset finance across low- and middle-income markets overall.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Commercial returns, not concessional subsidy, are already carrying the bulk of developing-market renewables risk.
insights.quote: Private investors are leading the way, supplying about 85% of the asset finance in these markets overall.

insights.claim: In low-income economies specifically, about 25% of renewable asset finance was supplied by development finance institutions, a far larger role than in middle-income markets.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Cuts to DFI budgets would bite hardest in the poorest markets while leaving middle-income deployment largely unaffected.
insights.quote: In low-income economies, about 25% was supplied by development finance institutions.

insights.claim: The European Union supplied more than 33% of foreign asset finance for renewables in low- and middle-income markets, while the US was the largest individual provider among nations.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Cross-border clean-energy finance remains anchored in EU and US institutions, tying developing-market build-out to their fiscal and political cycles.
insights.quote: Among blocs, the European Union supplied more than 33% of foreign asset finance, while the US was the largest individual provider among nations.

insights.claim: Both the European Union's and the US's foreign asset-finance totals were boosted by the development finance institutions headquartered in them.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Headline EU and US 'investment' figures partly reflect state-backed lenders rather than purely private appetite.
insights.quote: Both are home to major development finance institutions, which played a role in their fund totals.

insights.claim: US renewable-finance flows shifted toward India in 2025, while mainland China's fundings were concentrated in Asia Pacific.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Capital-provider geographies are splitting into regional spheres, a marker of financing blocs forming around clean-energy infrastructure.
insights.quote: US flows shifted toward India in 2025, with mainland China’s fundings concentrated in Asia Pacific.

insights.claim: Investor nationality in this analysis is assigned at deal level by comparing the location of the renewable asset with the headquarters of the investor providing debt or equity, and undisclosed investment is excluded entirely.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: The 'domestic capital' share depends on an HQ-based definition and omits undisclosed deals, so the true local share could differ.
insights.quote: Investor nationality is based on the location of the renewable energy asset versus the headquarters of the investor providing debt or equity financing to the asset.
